conventions.convention: The forward factorization is A = G ∘ F; reconstruction applies the G-regularizer first and the F-regularizer second. No general pseudoinverse product identity is assumed.

The convergence theorem assumes Countable Choice and a common positive singular system, with 0 < λ_j, μ_j ≤ 1 and the middle range-closure equality. Pseudoinverse compatibility is established for the specified exact datum under these hypotheses.
The source condition is x† = |A|^ν w = (A*A)^(ν/2)w, with ||w|| ≤ ρ, ρ > 0, ν₀ > 2, and 1 < ν ≤ ν₀ − 1. Qualification is expressed in singular-value powers s, corresponding to spectral powers s/2.

Both parameter sequences start at index 1 and have successive ratios in [θ,1). Selection uses the first qualifying residual index. Convergence is conditional on both indices existing for sufficiently small positive noise levels; exact data are nonzero.

The open problem concerns deterministic worst-case error for the specified two-stage stopping rule, with factors, filters, parameter sequences, and radius fixed; it does not assert optimality among all reconstruction procedures.

load_bearing.statement: For compact linear maps F:X→Y and G:Y→Z, set A:=G∘F. For spectral regularization families and a parameter rule (α,γ):(0,∞)×Z→(0,∞)², define Tδ(zδ):=R^F_{γ(δ,zδ)}(R^G_{α(δ,zδ)}zδ). First regularize G, then F; no general identity A†=F†G† is part of the definition.

Under Countable Choice, the stated normalized common singular system, source condition x†=|A|^νw with ||w||≤ρ and Ax†≠0, filter norm and qualification bounds, threshold inequalities, and first-crossing parameter rules, any sequence δ↓0 on which both selected indices eventually exist satisfies, for sufficiently small δ, ||x†−R^F_γ R^G_α zδ||≤C₁ρ^(1/(ν+1))δ^(ν/(ν+1))+C₂ρ^(2/(ν+1))δ^((ν−1)/(ν+1)), with constants independent of δ and ρ. For fixed ρ the reconstruction converges to x†.
